trust_decision.summary: Not a trust boundary: a lock-count invariant. AbstractTransactionManager.lock() increments lockCount and then runs prepareToSave() on every changed domain object; if prepareToSave throws, the count is never decremented, so the object stays locked (DomainObjectLockedException on later transactions/undo/close).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names OptionsDB, but OptionsDB is unchanged by the fix. An engineer would open it first, find no lock code there, and then move to the transaction manager in the same package.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API DomainObject.lock(String) via DomainObjectAdapterDB.lock (DomainObjectAdapterDB.java:258-260); also reached by DomainObjectAdapterDB.save (:530), saveToPackedFile (:568), GhidraFolderData.createFile (GhidraFolderData.java:1040), SynchronizedTransactionManager.addDomainObject (SynchronizedTransactionManager.java:67), lockForSnapshot (AbstractTransactionManager.java:101)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Ghidra/Framework/SoftwareModeling/src/main/java/ghidra/program/database/ProgramDB.java:2468-2476 (composite lock: super.lock then programUserData.lock; if the user-data lock throws from its prepareToSave, the program's own lock taken at :2469 is never released; super.unlock() at :2473 covers only a false return)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The published fix makes each transaction manager clean up after itself, so a solver can say ProgramDB just delegates and the base fix already covers it. In fact the program's own already-acquired lock still leaks when the user-data lock throws.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Locks are reentrant and counted: lockForSnapshot pre-increments lockCount so the nested lock("snapshot") skips prepareToSave and then decrements in finally. SynchronizedTransactionManager.addDomainObject takes the lock and then zeroes the joined manager's count. A fix that resets lockCount to 0, or decrements unconditionally, breaks the snapshot nesting and the save/unlock pairing; unlock() asserts lockCount != 0.

O6_input_shapes: any RuntimeException/Error thrown by a DomainObjectAdapterDB.prepareToSave override (default DomainObjectAdapterDB.java:266-273, DBTrace override Ghidra/Debug/Framework-TraceModeling/src/main/java/ghidra/trace/database/DBTrace.java:878-882)
multiple domain objects under a SynchronizedTransactionManager (loop over getDomainObjects())

O7_producer.where: prepareToSave -> updateMetadata -> saveMetadata (DomainObjectAdapterDB.java:592-594, :643-645; ProgramDB.java:2462-2465) is where the exception originates, but it is not a data producer in the schema/serializer sense

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ProgramDB.lock composite: program lock leaks if programUserData.lock throws (user-data prepareToSave exception)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Delegating wrapper; the base fix 'handles exceptions in lock()', so the wrapper looks safe
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other module (SoftwareModeling) and package from the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: getAndLockInUseDomainObjectForMergeUpdate: lock(operation) succeeds, then hasUncommittedChanges() true throws FileInUseException before the caller's inUseDomainObj is assigned, so the callers' finally unlockDomainObject(null) never releases the lock
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Versioned checkin/merge path (needs a repository/merge); 'uncommitted changes right after lock' looks impossible since there is no open transaction
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file (GhidraFileData; callers at :1281, :1624, :2110)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: forceLock: ++lockCount then terminateTransaction; if that throws (e.g. from domainObjectRestored/changeSet listeners), the count leaks and callers that rely on forceLock returning never unlock
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: forceLock is documented as a forced, destructive emergency path, and callers 'own' the lock afterwards

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SynchronizedTransactionManager.addDomainObject: the joined mgr is locked at :67; an exception before lockCount reset at :84 (e.g. clearTransactions) leaves it locked
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Internal join of transaction managers, rarely used, and the 'lock' here is a temporary trick

O8b_injection_room.sibling: move the lock acquisition so a throwing step (getContentHandler) sits between lock and try
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same lock-then-try pattern written by hand at several callers; easy to reorder by mistake

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a wrapper that does extra work after object.lock() before returning the hold
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AutoCloseable holder only protects once constructed; any work before 'new DefaultHold' leaks

O9_family: error-path resource release (unreleased lock / missing finally, CWE-460/667)

O10_build.project_tests: unknown: no tests in fix diff; Framework/Project and SoftwareModeling have JUnit suites but no specific transaction-manager lock test verified

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap prepareToSave in try/finally in AbstractTransactionManager.lock() (or catch inside OptionsDB) and stop, leaving the ProgramDB composite lock and the merge-update lock leak open.
